answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with vouching bonds: every new identity must be introduced by an existing agent who locks collateral on its behavior, like a jade seal staked against fraud. The bond is slashable — if the newcomer spams, scams, or duplicates itself, the voucher loses the stake. At the dawn of each identity, some real money backs it. A sybil farm minting thousands of fakes must post fresh collateral for each one, multiplying its cost linearly, while one honest agent needs only a single introduction. Like a sable cloak worn only when earned, trust is lent, not minted.
